target_customer: Nurses, especially travel nurses, as consumers of a banking app
problem: Nurses face student debt and irregular pay and lack a financial product built for their work, including early access to earned pay and refinancing.
business_model: Consumer fintech: banking app with earned wage access, student loan refinancing referral and travel nurse job data

founders.name: Shantanu Joshi
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by the YC page and by Vivian Health (September 2022), which said he would lead product and engineering work on financial products. Background not found in an opened source.

founders.name: Christopher Chang
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by the YC page and by Vivian Health (September 2022). Background not found in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Banking and earned wage access need partner bank, payments and compliance integrations, which are standard fintech engineering but with regulatory overhead for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Niche focus on nurses was a wedge, but the underlying services were commodity partner products and employer wage access platforms already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it. A nurse jobs marketplace, Vivian Health, struck a technology agreement with the founders in September 2022.

market_need_then: Nurses carry student debt and travel nurse demand surged in 2020 and 2021; no source quantified demand for the banking product itself.

identity.voice_and_tone: Vivian described it as a banking experience built from the ground up for nurses

branding.community_and_virality: A Lume newsletter addressed readers as 'Lumers' per a search snippet, but nothing else was found

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found, and many unrelated companies share the name Lume.

outcome_analysis: Lume reached the YC Summer 2020 batch with a banking app for nurses and, per aggregators, raised only about 130 to 150 thousand dollars. In September 2022 Vivian Health announced an agreement to use Lume's technology and hired both co-founders to lead product and engineering on financial products. Vivian did not describe a purchase of the company and the planned products were still under development, so this reads as a soft landing for the team rather than a venture outcome.
notes: Funding rests on aggregators: PitchBook reportedly 150K and CB Insights 130K total, investors Y Combinator and Esas Ventures (Soma Capital per PitchBook); amounts conflict so the round amount is null. YC and a listing say acquired by Vivian Health in 2022, but Vivian's own post describes an agreement to use Lume's technology; type acquisition follows the YC directory. Company site did not resolve (uselume.com not reachable from the session), so the site is treated as dead or unreachable. Competitors: the dated search returned only 2026 pages, so the list is empty. Other companies named Lume (data mapping, health) were excluded.
